feedback.problem:
The following table gives the values of functions $f(x)$ and ${f}^{′}(x)$ at some points. Find $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3).$

| **$x$** | $f(x)$ | ${f}^{′}(x)$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $4$ | $-9$ | $0$ |
| $5$ | $3$ | $-2$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse is

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(x))}.
$$

Substituting $x=3,$ we have

$$
({f}^{-1})^{′}(3)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))}.
$$

From the table, we obtain ${f}^{-1}(3)=5$ and ${f}^{′}(5)=-2.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}({f}^{-1})^{′}(3) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(5)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(-2)} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
